paper_metadata.title: Creep deformation and strength evolution mechanisms of a Ti-6Al-4V alloy during stress relaxation at elevated temperatures from elastic to plastic loading

evidence.quote: Creep deformation and strength evolution mechanisms of a Ti-6Al-4V alloy during stress relaxation at elevated temperatures from elastic to plastic loading
Previous studies of Ti-6Al-4V alloy with equiaxed microstruc- ture have confirmed that the creep strain rate in the SR is posi- tively correlated with the dislocation density introduced by loading
Ti-6Al-4V titanium alloy
The as-received material used in this study is Ti-6Al-4V extruded profile with a fully lamellar microstructure (Widmanstätten)

extruded Ti-6Al-4V alloy with lamellar microstructures
The as-received material used in this study is Ti-6Al-4V extruded profile
extruded Ti-6Al-4V alloy with lamellar microstructures
The as-received material used in this study is Ti-6Al-4V extruded profile with a fully lamellar microstructure (Widmanstätten) provided by BaoTi Group (China).

The different SR behaviors, YS evolutions and corresponding mechanisms of extruded Ti-6Al-4V alloy with lamellar microstructures under various stress levels (elastic and plastic regions) and temperatures have been investigated

evidence.quote: The subsequent SR stage facilitates interfacial diffusion and results in a higher fraction of granular β phases, leading to a further decrease in yield strength (YS).
The stress exponent calculated from SR curves at 700 and 750 °C ﬂuctuates between 2 and 3, proving the reasoning that dislocation creep plays a dominant role in SR at these temperatures
The combined effects of dislocation creep and bulk diffusion creep render the threshold stress low and relaxation rate high at 800–850 °C.
The pile-ups at the α/ β phase interfaces were formed due to mismatch of the slip planes to accommodate the slip incompatibility of the two phases.
σH-P is the contribution from Hall-Petch strengthening by α/ β interfaces
